html:
The Warumungu, also spelt Warramunga, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, around Tennant Creek in the middle of the continent. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours included the Kaytetye to the south, the Warlmanpa to the west and the Jingili and Wambaya to the north. The Overland Telegraph Line passed through their land in 1872, with a repeater station at Tennant Creek. The anthropologists Baldwin Spencer and Francis Gillen visited them in 1901 and wrote about their ceremonies.

A gold rush at Tennant Creek in the 1930s brought miners and a town, and the Warumungu were moved off their land onto a reserve to the north. They won back part of their country through land claims in later decades.
